He was brought in by the police, and in paragraph 2005 [as interpreted], you justified that or, rather, you link that up to your testimony. So you involve your son in paragraph 205, and I'm saying that that's not the way it was. I'm saying that it's actually the other way around. You are testifying here five years after Mauzer was killed. You are testifying in a very extreme way, falsely, and you are making off-handed allegations because your son is in trouble.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: You are simply engaging in a series of comments. This is very far from cross-examination. You know the difference between commenting, and pretending or purporting to give evidence, and asking relevant questions. I haven't heard a relevant question now for some time from you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In relation to this newspaper article that I'm just being shown to be put on the ELMO, I object against it. This is just a newspaper article from a Banja Luka newspaper, and it's going on about the son, and of the rest I can't really read because it's only in the B/C/S. I would object against the relevance of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the witness, himself, referred to some newspaper article which was turned out not to be true at the end of the day, so I don't see any point of putting those news articles to the witness. I'll consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something before you make your decision? May I say something before you make your decision?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, it was at your initiative that I showed the document. You said that if I wished to continue taking that line, that I had to come up with something. I am coming up with something, something that the witness, himself, referred to; that that was in the media, for instance. Your Excellency Judge Morrison, I agree that perhaps it hasn't been phrased as a question, but I'm presenting the case of the Defence here. I am actually presenting the position of the Defence, that is in contrast to what the witness has been claiming, but perhaps that needs to be done more skillfully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, you're cross-examining, Dr. Karadzic, and it has to be the Defence case can be put through asking relevant questions which indicate what the case is and test the witness's view of it. But simply making comments as you have been doing, first of all, it doesn't help us determine anything about the accuracy or credibility of the witness, and, secondly, it's not something we can take into account because it's simply a comment. It uses huge amounts of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, if I might refer to what I mentioned last week, if, when you put your suggestion to the witness, give him a chance to answer, yea or nay, and then put another one, so that in that way, your case is answered one way or the other by the witness, and it's on the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I refer you to what the witness stated today. It's page 44, line 14. He is said: "There was this big article that appeared one day that said that my son took part in Mauzer's murder directly. An investigation was conducted, and that I didn't want to interfere in any way. And the investigation concluded that he had nothing to do with it." Having heard this answer, there's no point of putting that newspaper article to the witness. It's totally a waste of time. You can prove that fact with other witnesses, if you have that. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, were you ever a threat to anyone's life?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Why? I don't see any reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Apart from that major, were you mixed up in other cases of police brutality?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by the word "brutality." I carried out police duties in extraordinary wartime circumstances, when I must admit we were not always able to limit ourselves to the regular means and methods as in regular peacetime police work. We were dealing with people who were armed, who did not choose their means to get to their objectives, so I don't know what you mean by "brutality." I'd like you to explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that. Let's see why you mixed up Tomo Kovac, then deputy minister and later minister of the interior of Republika Srpska. In paragraph 205 -- could we now see 1D3671. This is a submission against Dragan Andan, director of the Police Force of Republika Srpska. And in the first paragraph, we read: "In the past three years, Dragan Andan has continuously used his position at the Ministry of the Interior ..." And so on. And the last sentence in paragraph 2 reads: "Because of such conduct in Bijeljina, the police officers mutinied, and I, as the assistant minister, had the task of calming down the police officers, but they, as well as the relatives of fallen policemen, demanded that Andan not be allowed to enter the MUP and to have Mico Davidovic's unit expelled from Bijeljina." And then the third sentence in the next paragraph: "During the clearing up, an attempt on my life was organised by Mico Davidovic and Dragan Andan, but they only managed to damage the vehicle. The assassin fired at me from the Radical Party offices in Bijeljina." Do you know where that building where the Radical Party headquarters were is located, and do you know about this shooting at Tomo Kovac?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first I'm hearing about it. I never heard about it from anyone, let alone anyone saying that I was involved in such an attempt. I was a high-ranking police official. If I wanted to kill someone or do something against the law, I could have done it in a different way, a very different way, without getting personally involved. I was not involved in any of these things described here, but this is such rubbish that it doesn't deserve comment, really. It's completely beyond the pale, trying to connect me with an assassination attempt against Tomo Kovac. I don't know who made this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is an official submission to the Government of Republika Srpska, to the minister of the interior, written by Tomo Kovac and his assistant. Can we see the next page in Serbian. You see the last paragraph. In English, we need the next page. You see the last paragraph, where he says: "I warned the minister about responsibility, in view of the consequences on the citizens, because you can see that I cannot wash my hands of anything done by any lunatic. But we did deal, together with members of the service, with people like Andan, Karan, Tomic. We suspended, removed them and detained them." Is it true that you detained, suspended and removed members of the police?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not do any of these things. We discussed already that Andan was removed from the police. We discussed that in the Mico Stanisic case, and I don't see how and what I could have to do with all these persons, Andan, Karan and Tomic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 1D3668. If you need to see the signature, we can show you the last page of this, just the last page in Serbian, and then we can move on to 1D3668. Then one more page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the signature of Tomo Kovac?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 1D3668.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 11 September 1992, decision: "Andan, Dragan, shall temporarily be removed from the Ministry of the Interior of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina as of 11 September 1992." "Temporary removal," is that another synonym for suspension?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. He was suspended from the SUP, and we all know for what reason. At the Mico Stanisic trial, it was discussed why he was suspended. Perhaps the OTP has the documents that can be admitted into evidence, but I know that reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the reason?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I left Bijeljina, Dragan Andan remained as chief of the Security Centre in Bijeljina. I had gone to Pljevlja because of the same or similar problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was his sin?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me finish. I got a call from Dragan Andan saying that he had received orders from Minister Stanisic, that he had to go to Foca and work again with a part of his unit, to disarm paramilitary units. He went to the so-called Bosnian Villa in Belgrade where he was received by Mr. Stanisic, and when that meeting was over he called me again and said, They suspended me because I had refused to go to Foca. And when I had talked to him earlier, I had told him that they know about him coming to Foca, that there would be an ambush, and there could be problems. And when I asked him in that second conversation if that was the reason he refused, he said, yes, that was the reason. And later, when I went to Belgrade and returned from Pljevlja, from Montenegro, I found Mico Stanisic. I went to the SUP. Tomo Kovac was there as well. And they told me then they suspended him because Dragan Andan had, without authorisation, from the premises of the SUP, where seized objects are kept, he removed two or three -- those gambling machines - what do you call them? - you know -- yes, those gambling machines, and he placed them in some privately owned cafes and, of course, profited from it in some way. I told them that was the first time I was hearing about it, and I told them they were right, I would do the same if I determined that something like that had been done. So I supported Mico Stanisic and Tomo Kovac in that case. There's nothing controversial about that. And in subsequent proceedings, I believe Dragan Andan was a witness in the Stanisic case. On that occasion, I gave the same statement, the same evidence, and what can I say now? At first, I didn't know the real reason, and later I found out and I confirmed it. And in the Stanisic case, I said I had seen a document, an official document, stating that Dragan Andan had removed those gambling machines from official police premises and made a profit from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When did you return from Pljevlja and when did Stanisic tell you that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I have to tell you that while I was still in Pljevlja, when Dragan was suspended, I went to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. I found Mr. Tolimir there, as well as Petar Salapura, and told them that if they have any vacancies, they should take Dragan Andan to work for them. And I believe I went to Bijeljina at that time. I found Mico Stanisic and Tomo Kovac. Tomo was at the time his assistant or deputy. Mico Stanisic was no longer minister later, but Tomo Kovac remained. But at that time, he was in Bijeljina, and there was Cedo Kljajic present as well when we discussed this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But even though you heard that knowledge during the war, and you told Mico Stanisic and Tomo Kovac you were right, in your paragraph 114 of your statement, you still go on saying that Dragan Andan had been suspended because he had good intentions towards Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say what I've said before in my evidence. Dragan Andan, working in his job, as least as far as I was concerned, carried out his work impeccably. I did not notice, in this conduct, any sign of discrimination against any other national community, and he was extremely dedicated and committed to me, as his superior, and always followed orders. And I also have to say that Dragan Andan was not very well liked in the MUP of Republika Srpska. I believe he had had a conflict with Mico Stanisic even before the war. Mico confirmed that and Cedo Kljajic confirmed that, because when Cedo Kljajic suggested Dragan Andan became my assistant as a co-ordinator, then Mico Stanisic said, Why are you sending him, Cedo. You know who Dragan Andan is. He was involved with the Muslims. He mentioned some butcher, some football referee. And Mico said, I don't want to see him here in Sarajevo. And then Cedo said, I sent him to Brcko, to work in the organs, to help out, if necessary. And this relationship between Mico Stanisic and Dragan Andan is something I know nothing about. Why they couldn't tolerate each other, I don't know. But I confirm that in his job, Dragan Andan was a very good officer, and what he had done later is really something that I condemn. And I said, speaking to Mico Stanisic later, I would have done the same, I would have suspended him because of what he had done with those gambling machines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's come back to what is written here. Look at paragraph 114 of your statement as well. Mr. Davidovic, you know who appoints the chief of the Security Services Centre; it's the minister?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mico Stanisic, despite what you say, that they were in conflict even before the war, is it true that Mico Stanisic appointed Dragan Andan chief of Security Services Centre?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was appointed by Cedo Kljajic, and he signed his letter of appointment, his temporary appointment as acting chief of Security Services Centre. Cedo probably made that decision in agreement with Mico Stanisic, and the reason was probably that Dragan Andan had worked with us in Brcko, Zvornik and Bijeljina, and that's probably what motivated Mico Stanisic to give his consent for the appointment. It could have been -- it could not have been done without Mico.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So he was appointed because he was expected to work well, and you also received praise in your work. But despite the fact that you knew all this even during the war, in paragraph 114 you still state that he was suspended -- Dragan Andan was suspended because he was good to the Muslims, and you changed that only when Stanisic showed you the document, whereas here, in the statement given for my case, you had a chance to correct this, and you were banned -- and this theory that he was suspended because he was good to the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they had dealt with these details. If they had, I mean, the Prosecution, I would have shown them the statement I gave in Mico Stanisic's case. I put all the relevant facts there. This statement was prepared at a time when I did not know about this. The investigators, themselves, could have co-ordinated these statements. There was one member of the Trial Chamber in that case who asked me, Would you have suspended the man, knowing what you knew? I said I would. But I know -- I knew at the time there were some problems, and I thought, when he went to have that meeting in Belgrade, that he was suspended for some other reasons.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this document admitted, the one on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1408, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, 1409.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3669, can we please see that one now just to look at it briefly to see if that was the document you were presented concerning reasons for the suspension of Andan. 1D36 -- yes, 3669.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at this document. Is that the document you were shown during the Stanisic trial?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is. More or less, the essence is the same. It has to do with machines that were seized from the SJB depot.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have it admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1410, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 169 of your statement, you talk about Zuca, his arrest, and you say that five to six persons were arrested, they were all released about three days later, and that, as far as you remember, that you were already in Belgrade at the time, and that later on Zuca was indicted in Sabac and was sentenced to seven or eight years. Now, you say in paragraph 169 --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's in fact 168.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He realised this mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in 169, you say: [In English] "It was only because I was working in the Federal SUP, that I was able to achieve what I did." [Interpretation] And the sentence further down: [In English] "As a consequence of our achievement, Dragan Andan was dismissed from his post right after my return to Belgrade." [Interpretation] Then a bit further down, you say: [In English] "I can see at page 3 of this document, it says that Dragan Andan was temporarily suspended for illegal use of poker machines. I was not aware of this before. It shows that Stanisic removed Andan from his post for this reason, not because he was involved in disarming or arrest of paramilitaries." [Interpretation] Is -- that paragraph 169 of your statement, is that what it reads?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please wait a little bit. I have to find this paragraph. Everything is mixed, we skip and jump from one thing to another, so I cannot find my bearings.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, please let me read it. Yes. So what is contested here? Can you please repeat what you asked me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you can see that in the same paragraph, you stick to it that as a consequence of his successful work, Dragan Andan was dismissed from his post. And then you see, yourself, that in the same paragraph you say, yourself, that that was not the reason, but, rather, his criminal activities?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I told you how things developed and what happened. Now, what happened later about his suspension, this is something that I clarified in detail in the Stanisic trial. You're insisting on this once again. I described it then. I gave my testimony, and I also gave my statement about things as I was aware of them now. Dragan Andan informed me that Mico Stanisic suspended him, would not allow him to go on working. He didn't tell me that the reasons were the gambling machines, in the first place, but problems about his departure to Foca and earlier problems that there were between Mico Stanisic and some Muslims that Mico Stanisic had known. So that was a statement I gave at that moment, and later on there was clarification about the other documents which are referred to now, which were presented in the Mico Stanisic case. So I do not deny that that was the reason and that I would have suspended him as well. At the moment when I knew what was happening, this is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And Stanisic informed you --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Nothing else is actually said in the amalgamated statement. The witness has already, in the amalgamated statement, corrected his previous view as can be seen, and there is also reference to the document that he was looking at and saw that the gambling machine was actually the reason for the suspension.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I respond to this, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We have the witness's answer. We can proceed. Move on to your next question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, now please focus your attention on paragraph 54 of your statement. You say that you were with me and Mladic in Lukavica. What sort of meeting was that? Who was the chairman, and who was keeping the minutes?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not a meeting, it was not scheduled, it was not chaired by anyone. At the request of Petar Gracanin, who was my minister - there were intercepted conversations here - he informed me that I should go and report to Ratko Mladic and inform him whether I needed additional equipment, weapons or ammunition, that I should report to him, and that I had to report to Ratko Mladic, who was at the barracks in Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm just asking you if it was a meeting which Mladic, you and I attended.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was an informal conversation, because you suddenly showed up while I was talking with Ratko Mladic. You were not announced, and no one knew you would come. I think that even General Ratko Mladic didn't know that you would appear. Once you entered the room, we got up to greet you, and then you joined us in the conversation. The conversation couldn't have lasted for more than five to ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say: "I demanded of Mladic that measures be taken regarding the looting, the stealing of cars, and against criminals in the MUP of Republika Srpska." And so on. Was it a duty of the army, and how could you demand from Mladic to do something that is a police job?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came there and talked to General Mladic, at the beginning of our conversation, when he asked me what we were doing and where we were, I told him, among other things, that I noticed that there were many incidences of looting, robbery and so on, and that active-duty policemen and reserve policemen were doing that, that there were informal groups who broke into Muslims' apartments and homes, took out items. I had occasion to see, in front of a high-rise building, how they were hauling stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right, all right. I'm just asking you whether this was the duty of the police or the army to do that.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I informed him about this with the intention to have him know about that, as a general of the army, and to receive any sort of suggestion from him what we should do if we came across such people doing such things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Pause, pause. Yes, put your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Karadzic was present and a party to the conversation. Karadzic and Mladic confirmed that such things were happening and that it was quite noticeable, and that it could be changed. Mladic told Karadzic that it was hard to function with all this chaos. Karadzic's reply was that he would speak with Djeric and see what could be done. Djeric was the prime minister at the time; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Karadzic said that we should try and prevent the looting, but that there should be no arrests of Serbs or conflicts between them. Karadzic said that it was very important for Serbs not to fight one another, as it had been the case in the Second World War. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So at the moment, was I the head of Republika Srpska or the president?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you were.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have a look at D1406. If we can please see page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please read this, beginning with: "Considering ..."? This is your statement given to the Serbian MUP; correct? Is that the statement you gave to the Serbian MUP which we looked at a while ago?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please read the last paragraph, which begins with the word "Considering"?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Considering," is that what you mean, "that between April and September 1992, at the order of the leadership of Republika Srpska, I was involved in identifying and arresting war criminals who are Serbs, and disarming various Serbian paramilitary formations, as well as information that since 1992 I received frequent threats from the members of these groups, I conclude that this is provocation designed to compromise me as a character and as a member of the Federal MUP."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have a look at another document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the accused please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2741. I'm sorry, 65 ter 7442.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2900, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a report sent to the president of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina by Dragan Andan. Can we please see the last page. This is about what you and he were doing. This is the 29th of July. You were already in Bijeljina at the time, and he described to me what you were doing in Bijeljina. So please have a look at my comments. Can you please read to the Trial Chamber what is handwritten in Cyrillic at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it says: "Keep --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Enforcing"?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: " ... enforcing order ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: " ... and the rule of law."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Keep enforcing order and the rule of law ." I apologise. And this is your signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a document which the Prosecutor showed you during the proofing; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the first time I see it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have a look at something from your statement, paragraph 101 of your statement, where you say: [In English] "I do not know whether the handwritten note, 'Keep enforcing order and the rule of law,' 2nd of August, 1992, Radovan Karadzic," in ERN so and so, "comes from Radovan Karadzic or not. This is the first time I see it, but I can say that I or Dragan Andan never received any support or recognition from the work we were doing." [Interpretation] So you have seen it, but you doubt it; correct.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it now, but Dragan never told me that he ever received that with your signature and that you wrote a comment. I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Put in paragraph 101, you confirm that you have seen this document?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure whether I saw it. It was not shown to me here by the Prosecution, and I don't believe I saw it earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now please see 1D3734.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You should know I had the occasion to be presented with many documents at the first and the second trial, and now, so it's difficult for me to say with any certainty whether this document was presented to me or not. You have to understand, it's really a heap of documents.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 264 in e-court of this document, 1D3734. Or, rather -- yes, yes, that's the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were asked here, in the second question from the top of the page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You better tell the witness what this document is about. This seems to be the transcript in the Krajisnik case.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, it's the transcript from the Krajisnik trial. I thought the witness should be given a chance to see that and if he remembers it. It's Monday, the 13th of June: [In English] "So I take it there that you blamed the SDS for losing your job as chief of police?" [Interpretation] Then you say, it's line 18: [In English] "Had I wanted to join in, I would have done it. I was offered promotion." [Interpretation] You were saying that you were offered to become a member of SDS and that you were offered a promotion. Is it correct, Mr. Davidovic, that elections were held in November 1990 and you remained in your position until June or July of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the elections were completed, after less than a month or two, once the Republican MUP came into power, I was relieved of my post and Predrag Jesuric was assigned to my post. Before this replacement and the change of complete relationships, which were a consequence of elections, when the party was registered, as it was registered as an association of citizens rather than a political party, it was only after the election that a law was adopted according to which political parties could be formed. That was the multi-party system which was then established, so parties could now be registered. And up until that time, the law which was in force stipulated that only associations of citizens could be registered with the organ of Internal Affairs. So if it was from Bijeljina, it had to be registered at the Bijeljina SUP, and then the statute would be established, the Executive Board, the members who were in the governing bodies, and so on. Then a proposal would be submitted and what was then called the Association of Citizens would be registered. Later on, it was changed into a political party. At the moment when there were preparations ongoing for such a preparation, Predrag Jesuric, who was organising all this in Bijeljina, talked to me frequently. And, among other things, he offered me to join the SDS party, saying that once the party came into power, that it would offer me a better and more adequate position, that I would be promoted and so on, but I did not accept that. We were in two different worlds, how we saw me and my possible position on the political scene at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you a sworn and firm Communist at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had been a member of the party. Once the League of Communists ceased to exist, I was never a member of any another political party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Your answer here: [In English] "Had I wanted to be a member ..." [Interpretation] And so on and so forth: [In English] "... any party that is called Serbian Democratic, et cetera, Serbia, sounded like something which was not progressive." [Interpretation] What is the origin of your disgust? Does it have to do with your membership in the League of Communists or what?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was never a supporter of any national party. Any kind of expression of ethnicity was something very conservative, from my point of view, because if someone highlights only one ethnic group or one nation, I do not want to talk to such people. I do not belong to their ranks, and I have to tell you that I never defined myself that way, as to whether I belonged to one ethnicity or nation or another. I belonged to the Serb people. I was born a Serb. I belonged to that culture. That is my identity. Everyone can identify themselves as they wish, but I am not disputing anyone else's right, any other ethnic or religious group. Everyone should have their own customs and traditions. But this very name or prefix, "Serbian," means that this is a mono-ethnic community that I could not belong to. This does not have to do with belonging to the Communist Party. This has to do with my attitude towards people. I never distinguished among people on the basis of their ethnicity. That is below any kind of civilisational level that I find acceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. It may not be that important, but while we are on this document, shall we show the witness page 147 in e-court of this document, the transcript, the last footage. It is 0658, page 147. It's about the document which contains Dr. Karadzic's signature, because you said you didn't remember whether you had seen this document before. It's in the middle of this, a question from Mr. Hannis from the Prosecution. The question is like this at line 14: "Assuming for purpose of my next question that that is Mr. Karadzic's signature, saying, 'Keep on enforcing the rule of law' it would seem to indicate that there was approval from him for the work that you and Mr. Andan had done in Bijeljina." And then your answer was: "I did not get a raise or no support in any way. I must admit I did not know about this, and I don't know whether this came from Radovan Karadzic. I mean, this is the document that I had not seen before, and I don't know." Now, do you remember having seen that document at the time of your evidence -- your giving evidence in the Krajisnik case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now that I've looked at this statement, I know that I've seen it. Please do not hold it against me. I cannot recognise the document. There were vast amounts of documents that were shown to me, so it's hard for me to be able to tell each and every time. When I came for the first time, I told the OTP that it's hard for me to remember exact dates and names, but basically I know what I did, and that is why I'm talking about what I did. That is why I keep repeating myself. I was not inventing anything. I was not saying things that were not true in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Davidovic. Rest assured, nobody holds it against you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we admit these two pages?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we give the number? D ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1411.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at 1D3646.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You sent a report to the minister about your activity in Republika Srpska; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, several reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the first report go on the 8th of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall. I should take a look. I cannot remember, especially not dates.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a version in Serbian too, so could we please have both.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that your first report, the 8th of August; that is to say, after your mission?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. Please allow me to have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the last page so that Mr. Davidovic can see his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now go back to the beginning. So everybody can read this, so I don't need to read it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say what you did. You headed the Brigade of the Federal SUP, and you were there to establish law and order, the normal functioning of organs of the interior; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then it says that every day, the population was being mistreated, irrespective of ethnic background; also, that there was robbery, looting of privately-owned and socially-owned property; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Further on, it says because of the illegal functioning of the organs of the interior and because of the terror of the paramilitary units in the territory of the CSB Bijeljina, masses of the population left, Muslim and Serbian, from the territories of Brcko, Bijeljina and Zvornik municipalities; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page. I think that it has to be the next page in English, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says, around the middle of the paragraph, you can see "867," the number 867, the number of reserve policemen, and that's how we're going to identify it. It's fine now. In the middle of the second paragraph in Serbian, it says employees of the milicija during the curfew, together with the military police, took over complete control, and in that period they prevented the commission of any kind of crimes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was actually the next page in English, wasn't it? In Serbian, it says: "Firm co-operation has been established with the corps command of the Serb Army and members of the military police in carrying out their joint tasks. And as for our work, organs of the local authorities were continuously informed and consulted about our work." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The last sentence down there, it says: "For example, after we arrived in the territory of the CSB Bijeljina --" Can we have the next one; in English too: "Not a single killing was committed as a result of inter-ethnic altercations."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Second bullet point: "There was no armed robbery."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Third bullet point: "Preventive operative work uncovered a number of groups involved in organised crime ... they were arrested and placed under investigation or expelled from the area of the CSB Bijeljina." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at the one further down: "The special unit carried out all its activity with the professional team of the Ministry of the Interior of the BiH, and in many cases they operated together with the Army of the Serb Republic of BiH." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the page that is three pages ahead. It says "7" in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Through a prepared and organised action, synchronised with the MUP of the SR BiH, the Special Unit very successfully, and without loss of human life ..." It is actually page 9 in English. "... disarmed all paramilitary locations in the area of the CSB Bijeljina." Does the CSB Bijeljina include Zvornik and Brcko and all of Semberija.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the entire part of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Zvornik is not included in the transcript. Lopare, Ugljevik. Can you tell us all of that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brcko, Bijeljina, Ugljevik, Lopare, Zvornik, Bratunac, Srebrenica, Sekovici, Milici. That is that area. However, we only dealt with three, Bijeljina, Brcko and Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So they disarmed members of the paramilitary formations that were engrossed in criminal activity, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please bear in mind for the court reporter as well, not -- in addition to the interpreters, please slow down when you read out something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "We arrested those who were engaged in crime, and they will have criminal proceedings instituted against them, and they will be prosecuted. They were returned to the FRY if they were nationals of the FRY, whereas local persons were deployed in regular units of the Serb Republic of BiH." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Vuckovic brothers, the leaders of the Yellow Wasps, were they nationals of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then you say here: "The special unit displayed a high degree of professionalism, efficiency and responsibility, for which they received commendations from the political organs in charge." It's the next page in English. "... and in these towns, we were welcomed as the liberators of Bijeljina, Zvornik and Brcko." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this report be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1412, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that this operation was commended at sessions of the Assembly of Republika Srpska, too?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was informed through some MP that there was a parliamentary debate, and what was mentioned was that we did our police work extremely well, and that that is the way each and every municipality should be dealt with, and that this resounded favorably in the public. However, when a specific conclusion was supposed to be passed to continue such activity, it was not actually adopted, first of all, because Speaker Krajisnik was against it. He said, Let us not arrest each other. So that subject was not discussed any further. At least that's what Micic told me, an MP from Republika Srpska. He said, People, I can just tell you that as for Mico Davidovic and people like him, we are going to make statues of them and keep them in the MUP for everyone to remember, and that that was the end of that debate and that there was no effect further on. Everything continued as previously. And once we withdrew, things got even worse.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, I looked at the entire transcript of Assembly sessions. The transcript includes even situations when people coughed. Mr. Krajisnik did not say that. Did you see that transcript? Did the Prosecutor show you that transcript that would confirm Mr. Krajisnik said that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one showed that to me. It was Micic, the MP, who told me about this. However, the first time I mentioned him in the Krajisnik trial, he did not wish to respond; also not in relation to some other documents and individuals.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get some names. Did you mention some names of individuals, Mr. Davidovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I said Micic. That was the name of the republican MP from Bijeljina. He said that to me. Now, whether that was true or not, whether he wanted to say that to me in order to show me that he was trying to point out what a good job I was doing or something, that I cannot say now. I just know what it was that he had said to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, is it correct that there were laws according to which you did what you did in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all the laws that were in force in the former Yugoslavia were still in force, and we acted on the basis of these laws. That gave us the right and authority to bring persons into custody, to file criminal reports, and to bring to justice persons who had committed murders, looting, robbery, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the Assembly did not need to pass any new laws or bills, is that right, it was just a commendation in view of that operation; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I have to say just one more thing. When I arrived in Zvornik, the provisional government suspended all republican and federal laws, and they ordered that it was only their decisions that would be valid. They placed themselves above any law, and that was made public in some Official Gazette of Zvornik, I don't know which one, though. So they actually authorised themselves only to do whatever they wanted, and they annulled all laws.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, you know about state administration. You know that the government annuls wrongful decisions made by municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it was not a new enactment before the Assembly, no new bill was proposed. There was a discussion. The operation was welcomed, then received praise; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I don't want to move to a new subject just before the break. Do you agree that we do that after the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll have a break, Mr. Davidovic, for an hour and resume at 1.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.26 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, we should now move to the subject of Yellow Wasps. That was one of the greatest, if not the greatest, operation which ended your mission in Republika Srpska? In paragraph 142 of your statement, last passage, it says: "We prepared the documents, submitted criminal reports to the Military Prosecutor in Bijeljina, but as soon as we withdrew from that region, all the proceedings were terminated and they were released." Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at 65 ter 7284.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This Exhibit P2905, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here - we can see the Serbian version - that the Lower Court in Bijeljina, on the 28th of August, with the Investigating Judge Biljana Simeunovic, et cetera, et cetera, concerning the crime of aggravated theft from Article 148, made the following ruling: "Detention against the accused, Vojin Vuckovic, known as Zuco, Rade Tanackovic," and other names, "is hereby suspended"?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There is no Dusko here; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see Vojin Vuckovic, not --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There is no Dusko Vuckovic, known as Repic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because the report is for aggravated theft and theft. As for the charge of murder, that was filed with the Military Prosecutor's Office, because a decision was then in effect that war crimes should be dealt with by military courts, whereas general crimes would be dealt with by the State Security Service. That's why this criminal report was filed in this form.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So they were reported, according to you, and suspected and accused of theft. It says detention is suspended. Can we see page 2 to see why detention -- or, rather, remand in custody is terminated. It says: "As follows from the above, the Public Prosecutor does not find there is sufficient grounds for detention at about 200 hours on 29 August 1992, it will have been a month since the date and the hour the detention started; that is to say, the length of time the accused can be detained pursuant to Article 197, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Code will have expired." Do you agree, then, that they were remanded in custody as long as it was lawful, and they were released when this dead-line expired, or just before it expired?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't agree with this suggestion. You have to clarify this case from the beginning. You showed me earlier a criminal report against these persons, if you remember. I'll tell you the details why this case was not dealt with and how they avoided prosecution. When we were dealing with the Yellow Wasps in Zvornik, on that day the prosecutor who was in Zvornik packed up his things, locked up his office, and went to the front-line. He volunteered to be a soldier on the front-line, not to be at the Prosecutor's Office any longer. So he was gone, and we had to file the criminal report to the Basic Prosecutor's Office in Bijeljina. This Prosecutor's Office made a decision several days later that they do not have jurisdiction because the case happened in Zvornik, which was correct, so they rejected the criminal report, sent it back to the MUP, saying that they should file it with the Prosecutor's Office in Zvornik. We did take it to Zvornik, and the report lay there for 30 days without being dealt with by anybody. It was just lying in a drawer. There was no prosecutor. So these 30 days, while we, as policemen, were in charge, expired, and all these days that they spent in remand have expired. And the question arose, what to do with them. Pressures were exerted that they be released. I was told later that it was Karadzic and Krajisnik who exerted that pressure, because I inquired. And what happened next? When the district republic prosecutor ordered that the Basic Prosecutor's Office in Bijeljina should take up the case, then the prosecutor in Bijeljina, who is not mentioned in preamble to this decision, if you would give us back the first page, it is said they are charged with aggravated theft, and remand for that kind of crime is allowed up to six months. But since nobody was working on the case, they had been remand for 30 days already, they had to be released, and, therefore, they found a solution. Article 197, paragraph 1, allows the accused to be charged only with theft; not aggravated theft or robbery, just theft. And remand for that kind of crime is allowed only up to 30 days. So they were released, they were free. The case file remained in the drawer of the Prosecutor's Office in Bijeljina. It was never taken up again. They left the remand prison, and nobody ever took that case up again. That's the entire problem with this case. In fact, the Prosecutor's Office changed the legal qualification from aggravated theft into simple theft. That's how they shortened the allowed remand in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says detention is suspended, and you are saying that, furthermore, the whole case was abandoned?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Detention was suspended. The case was left sitting in a drawer, and it was never prosecuted again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 1D3659.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You filed a criminal report only for aggravated theft; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For aggravated theft and robbery. Those are serious crimes. The Prosecutor's Office changed that into the qualification of simple theft.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at this document, 14 September 1992. The Basic Public Prosecutor's Office in Bijeljina is writing to the investigating judge in Bijeljina, requesting an expansion of the investigation against Dusko Vuckovic, also known as Repic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Article 148, aggravated theft; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here, "aggravated theft."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have a translation in the Office of the Prosecutor. We will provide it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we put it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see, Mr. Davidovic, that a request is made here to expand the investigation into aggravated theft from 28th June to 29 July? He was included in this investigation, although he was not in that first group; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next page. You said you transferred this to the Military Prosecutor's Office; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: See why the military prosecutor sent it back to the regular prosecutor. [In English] Yeah, okay. [Interpretation] The Military Prosecutor's Office returned this criminal report, explaining that the reported person, Dusko Vuckovic, cannot be treated as a member of the Serbian Army of the Serbian Republic, and that unlike other persons named in the report, he did not belong to the regular armed forces. So he was accused of theft, reported to the Military Prosecutor's office. The Military Prosecutor's office explained that he was not a soldier and returned it back to the regular Prosecutor; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I give a clarification?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it say that this name of this person is being included with the other names?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just give one more clarification about this passage that begins with the words: "Military Prosecutor's Office"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By all means, Mr. Davidovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Military Prosecutor's Office is terminating this because they explained, he was not a member of the Serbian Army. From what I know and from the documents shown me by the Prosecutor's Office - I mean by the OTP - we can see that those were members of the Territorial Defence Staff in Zvornik. The Territorial Defence Staff gave them their weapons and equipment and paid their salaries as two members of the armed forces they had under them. This claim by the Military Prosecutor's Office they were not members of the army means they were not militarily engaged in military units at that time, and they're not even treating them as a military unit, but as a paramilitary unit. And that's how it ends, that's how the case ends. Nothing was prosecuted in this case later, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As far as you know. But you say the Military Prosecutor's Office terminated the case. It didn't. It returned it to the civilian prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But they -- I mean, the Military Prosecutor's Office considered they had no jurisdiction. They returned it to the civilian prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was not termination.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained they returned it to the civilian Prosecutor's Office in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1413, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 65 ter 667. Could we see the next page in Serbian. Can we see page 3 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 16 November 1992. Is this an invitation to an expert witness, Milenko Tomic, in the case of Vuckovic et al?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see that it is a summons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So in the month of November, work continues on that case at the Court in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that from this summons.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1414, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 1D3655.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Lower Court in Bijeljina is writing to the 1st Municipal Court in Belgrade on 24 December 1993; requests to question an accused. Before this Court, criminal proceedings of investigation are underway against the accused, Vojin Vuckovic, Rade Tanackovic and others; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Signed: "Investigating Judge Biljana Simeunovic"?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D1415, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 65 ter 18846. Is this a Rule 70 document? Maybe it should not be broadcast. We don't have to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it is a Rule 54 bis document. But at the moment, I can't really see what is redacted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the redacted version --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... There is a redacted version, Your Honour, under that number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The redacted version is Exhibit P2818, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree -- page 3, please, without being broadcast. Do you agree, Mr. Davidovic, that this Centre of the State Security Sector, already on the 2nd of July, 1992 -- can we see page 2 in Serbian. In e-court, that means the first page in Serbian. The beginning, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, do you remember having been shown this document when examined by Madam Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Yes, I know about this document. I'm not going to mention the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Don't tell the names.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know. I've been shown this, and I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, they were charged with looting in Zvornik from 28 June until 29 July, and we see here that in the beginning of July, the process of investigation by this State Security Centre had already begun against these people. The State Security Service is displaying an interest and conducting interviews, investigating the activities of this group; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we mention the place where this State Security Department is from? Oh, we can see it. It's not redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the State Security Department from Valjevo is already conducting investigation, even before the period when they were looting, or, rather, during that period, investigative activities were already being carried out against this group; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not an investigative activity. It has not been approved by any relevant organ. This is just a note of authorised officials who are submitting that to their superior organ about information they have. It is initial information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Initial information; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, which is submitted to the relevant organ, and in order to prosecute someone, to initiate proceedings. Then it's a later stage of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please have a look at 1D3665 so that we can also see first whether there are any restrictions with regard to this document. 1D3665. I think there are no reasons. We do not need to broadcast this, just in case, though I think there are no reasons not to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it say here that on the 14th of December, 1992 - that's the text - and then the 7th of December, 1992, Mali Zvornik, Risto Zaric, a member of the National Security of the Republika Srpska MUP from Zvornik, informed me about extremist activities from Vojin Vuckovic, Zuca, from Umka, in the area of Podrinje, and other operative information?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have a translation. It's just been printed for the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm just wondering why the Defence could not get the translation in advance, while the Prosecution has it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, this is a huge case and our forces are really small, immeasurably smaller than the Prosecution has at its disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As pointed out several times, it cannot be an excuse. We'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Davidovic, that this is a case of co-operation between the State Security Department in Valjevo and officials of State Security from Republika Srpska? They are exchanging information about this group in December 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot hear. Yes, now I hear you. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So do you agree that in December 1992, the Valjevo RDB is co-operating with a high-ranking official who is a member of the National Security of Republika Srpska in collecting information about this group?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that Zaric went to Mali Zvornik and informed members of the State Security Service of the Republic of Serbia about information he had from Republika Srpska about persons who were citizens of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see item 2 on page 2: "Other volunteers ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it say down here, under item 1: "Other volunteers from the area of Republika Srpska, Dusan Vuckovic, son of Milan, also known as Repic"? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. If you could assist us, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, as to the confidentiality of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I see no reference to anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1416, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D3667, please. 1D3667, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the same office, RDB Valjevo, once it had collected information and carried out some activities, filed a criminal report with the District Prosecutor's Office in Sabac against Vuckovic, Dusan, also known as Repic, so he's number 1 now, and number 2 is Vujin Vuckovic, Zuco?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Because there is grounds to suspect that as co-perpetrators, they committed the crime -- war crimes against civilians? And can we see the next page, please. Under Article 142 of the Criminal Code of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and Dusan Vuckovic individually committed the crime of rape, and so on and so forth, unlawful arrest, and everything else is listed here; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D1417, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So nothing was terminated. Investigation is just being expanded, and so is the indictment; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Can we now please see 1D7375.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please clarify why I said that it's not correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I am satisfied with any of your answers. You say it's not so, but the document says it is.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason I say that is weighty, and I think the Trial Chamber should be aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, for the crimes which he undoubtedly committed, and it is known in Serbia that he did. And there was later information provided by Zaric, who was in Zvornik at the time when the crimes were committed, and who was familiar with the procedure of filing criminal reports against them. In Bijeljina, the procedure was terminated after 30 days, and they were released from custody. What was the basic condition for the Prosecutor's Office, once a criminal report is filed, to say that there are grounds for keeping someone in custody? The first reason is that the person cannot leave the site where a crime was perpetrated -- or, rather, the area. He has to be there. And what happened in Bijeljina was that the same person was acquitted and charged with a different crime, which is qualified differently. After that, there were reports sent to Belgrade from the Court that they are looking for information and so on. So now, 15 or 20 years later, we have the question: Why was this not prosecuted? It was, but we couldn't reach him. He had gone to Serbia, so he was out of reach. But why did he leave for Serbia? That was a mistake. He was released from custody. And why, who ordered that? That's the essential issue. It's true that after that, Serbia collected information, initiated proceedings against him in Sabac, but only after so many years and only after all the other crimes that had already been committed. And we had him in custody for the crimes he had committed right there on the spot. And this Zaric, who is working as a highly-ranking official, was also there. He informed the Serbian MUP, but he did not inform the Court, the organ that he should work with and to which he should submit reports. This is why I'm trying to say what the mistakes were made, procedural mistakes. The case was transferred to Serbia, but they were set free. The essence is that pressure was exerted on the Prosecutor's Office. They were set free. And when the public began to discuss this, when the newspapers reported about what was happening in Zvornik, then they couldn't pass over it in silence. They had to prosecute him in Serbia, they had to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted? It's already been admitted. All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Davidovic, you arrested all these men. You reported them, you drew up criminal reports. Why didn't you report a war crime?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did report a war crime to the Military Court. A war crime is prosecuted on the basis of a decision made by the government - I'm not sure which ministry at the time - namely, that the State Security should process war crimes and file criminal reports. And Public Security is in charge of aggravated theft and such crimes, and war crimes are prosecuted by military courts. This is why it happened this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you were aware of a war crime and you reported it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had to be aware, and we had to report it. Why was it prosecuted? These were the first cases in Republika Srpska which were prosecuted, the first reports that were written about someone who committed this sort of crime.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have a look at paragraph 141 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says: "In the reports and statements which we took, we did not take any other information about those relating to theft and robbery. That was what we investigated, but we didn't know that before these thefts and robberies, they had also committed murders. They did murder a group of civilians at Celopek, and they got that report from MUP in Zvornik, and they were identified in that report and described as people who are prone to killings ..." And so on and so forth. So you only investigated their robbery and you reported them for robbery, and you wonder that the army sent it back to the civilian judiciary, and you wondered that they were released from custody, but you did not report them for war crimes?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I was with my unit --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, I know where you were. Did you report them because they committed a war crime?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please allow me. I spent a month there. In that one month, we arrested, in additional to the Yellow Wasps, Arkan's group in Bijeljina, the murderers of Salih Hukic in Bijeljina. We also processed cases in Brcko, the Yellow Wasps --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, we would be grateful --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Red Beret --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, hear him out. I said this to you several times. Don't interrupt while the witness is answering your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need another two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He's not answering my question, Your Excellency. That wasn't my question. My question is Article 141. It only relates to Vuckovic and the Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, we were in charge of arresting these people and establishing law and order, professional services which were working as part of the SUP; that is to say, the Security Services, the Crime Prevention Service. These were the departments which are in charge of specific areas. I was not specifically charged with taking statements or writing criminal reports. I oversaw activities of disarming paramilitaries, and I was interested in knowing how far they got in taking statements, collecting information, and filing criminal reports. I wanted to know what happened with this case later on, but I couldn't physically or in any other way manage to process so many cases and file criminal reports during 25 days that I was there. I arrested and disarmed paramilitary formations, the dogs of war, criminals, thieves, murderers, and that was the reason why I worked in this way. And then I handed it over to the service of the Ministry of the Interior, headed by Stanisic and later on by Kovac, so that they would work on collecting other facts which would help to throw light on other crimes, such as thefts, and murders, and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Davidovic. This is not contested, and we were grateful to you for that and we expressed that publicly. The question is this: You're accusing the judiciary of Republika Srpska that they did not act as you expected, and you say that you reported a war crime and that they set him free.
