However, you reported him for only having committed aggravated theft, and this is what paragraph 141 of your statement says; that at the moment, you were not aware of murders, nor were you collecting any other information, except information relating to theft?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, let me go back to the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do not justify yourself.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not justifying myself to you. We were just establishing what they did. That's what I was doing at the moment. I took them in for aggravated theft, and the aggravated thefts were recorded, and that was submitted to the Prosecutor's Office. In the meantime, we also learned that in the same area, they also committed war crimes. There was also a report about that, it had to be submitted to one or the other of the relevant organs, to the MUP or Mico Stanisic. On the day when we were having briefing in Zvornik with him, he was informed about the detail that the same persons had committed war crimes. We were told that the war crimes are processed by the State Security, or the Military Prosecutor's Office, and that we should only submit criminal reports for aggravated theft and such crimes. So we didn't do that because there were other relevant organs. We were doing what was possible at the time so that people would be remanded in custody. When someone is remanded in custody, in the meantime, new information is collected, and the request to include new crimes is also added.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please slow down for the benefit of the court reporting. Yes. Could you start again: "When people are remanded in custody ..."?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once people are remanded in custody, then all information and facts about them are collected; that is to say, whether they committed aggravated thefts, robberies, rape, murder, war crimes, and so on. This is part of processing these persons. And people who are experts for that do that. There is the State Security Department. There is the Public Security Department which is in charge of crime prevention. So whoever works in these services works on these tasks. They collect facts and information so that the existing criminal report can be expanded with new information. That's the logical procedure, rather than releasing people from custody, without waiting for the final results, to check what information is available about such persons. I'm not attacking the judiciary of Republika Srpska. I'm just talking about specific cases that they were in charge. There were others. I could also give you other examples of cases which were not processed. Murders were committed, people were then released from custody, and these cases were only completed a few years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we say that paragraph 141 of your statement is correct or not? You investigated it, but you didn't know about the murders?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't put it that way, that we didn't know about the murders. We just did not deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us read it literally.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, when we look at page 52 in the English, it says: "But we did know that prior to those thefts and robbery, they had also been committing murders." It says they did know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the clarity, why don't we pull up the Krajisnik transcript. It has a reference to the transcript in Krajisnik, so let's see what he did say at the time. This is a summary of his evidence given in Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let's do that. The transcript page is -- I think it's 1D3734 - that's the e-court number - and transcript page, page 14313.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, in which language did you give your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Serbo-Croatian -- or, rather, Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said here -- if you allow, I will read it: [In English] "We did not take any other data, except for that theft and robbery. That was what we were looking into. But we did know that prior to those thefts and robbery, they had also been committing murders. I'm not talking about mass murder, but they did murder a group of civilians at Celopek, and I got that report from the MUP in Zvornik." [Interpretation] Why didn't you report murders in the criminal report you filed?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will go back to the beginning again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, that has been answered, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now please see 1D3735. In e-court, it's page 67, and in English, page 67 in e-court, please, from the Stanisic/Zupljanin case. Investigating Judge Biljana Simeunovic testified there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of this, and have you known this woman?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that woman quite well, and I know that she was a witness. I don't know the details, but I know that she was a witness in this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And she signed the decision to release these men from custody after the expiry of 30 days; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us look at this question: [In English] "Were you able, at certain periods, to communicate with, for instance, Pale? "A. I think there was ever -- there was never any need for me to communicate with Pale. I never called them, so I can't tell you much about that."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are we on the correct page?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. It's on page 67 in e-court, lines 7 to 19. Judge Biljana Simeunovic, lines 7 to 19: [In English] "Now, back in August 1992, if you had received this statement or any information from the civilian or military police about these crimes at the Celopek Cultural Centre, what would you have done, what actions would have you taken with regard to your criminal investigation in this matter? "A. Well, for one, if I did receive -- if I had received this, and I didn't, and now we're just hypothesising here, so seeing that this was handled by the military police and knowing that this individual was detained probably pursuant to a ruling by the Military Court, I would first get in touch with the prosecutor, or, rather, with the president of my Court, we would then discuss it in the collegium, and I am certain that we would have taken some steps and this person would not have been released from custody." [Interpretation] So the investigating judge that is in charge of the investigation knows only what you wrote for her. She did not know about the war crimes committed; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what she stated. What did you want her to state, that she knew about it and that she didn't do anything about it? Do you know that she's a judge in the war crimes tribunal in Bosnia and Herzegovina? She had to say that. That was the only way she could have protected herself, to say that she had acted appropriately, whereas facts say otherwise.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 140 in e-court, can we have a look at that now, from line 9 until line 13. I read it a moment ago. I can do it again: [In English] "Were you able at certain points to communicate with, for instance, Pale? "A. I think there was ever -- there was never any need for me to communicate with Pale. I never called them, so I can't tell you much about that." [Interpretation] Do you see, Mr. Davidovic, that you did not tell the truth, not to say that you lied? Somebody intervened with this lady judge.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I would not be saying that kind of thing. I came from the inspectors who worked on that case and who worked in the Office of the Prosecutor. Obviously you are trying in every possible way to say that you did not know about that. Now, who asked for these persons to be released from custody? Why was it insisted upon that persons who had serious criminal reports filed against them be released and have what they did treated as mere theft? How are their crimes being re-qualified? How are they being set free? All of this that followed was just formal work of the Court to justify what had happened. Now, that I lied, whether pressure was exerted or not, well, you can see, yourself, that pressure was being brought. They were being released, assistance is being sought from Serbia, and many years later Serbia was instituting proceedings because there was a great deal of pressure coming from the public.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Mr. Karadzic put his question while the witness was still answering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your question was overlapped so that it was not heard by the interpreters. But, Mr. Davidovic, in your answer, you said: "Why was it insisted upon that persons who had serious criminal reports filed against them be released?" What serious -- what criminal report are you referring to? And when you say "serious criminal reports," what did you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Theft and aggravated theft, that is what is referred to in the first criminal report that was filed with the Court. When detention, 30-day detention, was ordered, that was what was written in the criminal report, and then later on it was re-qualified so that they would be released.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3790. [In English] Sorry, I heard you earlier saying, Thank you. [Interpretation] 1D3790.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, do you see that this is a list of persons who are banned from entering the Serb Republic of BH? Number 1 is Vojin Vuckovic, Zuco, and the second one is Dusan Vuckovic, Repic. Do you see this list?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the first time I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the other names? You recognise some of them, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Davidovic, that Republika Srpska, only on the 13th of August, changed its name -- or, rather, from the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, it changed its name into Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know these dates, and I have not kept abreast of all of these political decisions. I'm not sure. I cannot tell you anything with precision.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted? If we go all the way up until the end, there are 42 persons here who are banned from entering Republika Srpska. Actually, can we please look at the last page. 42, can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1418, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon. Who banned these persons from entering; the BH, or Serbia, or Republika Srpska? I haven't seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's why I asked you whether you knew that on the 13th of August -- or, rather, up until the 13th of August, Republika Srpska was called the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is to say, this was issued before the 13th of August.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who issued this? Was it Serbia, or Republika Srpska, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How could Serbia ban entry into Republika Srpska? This is a document of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's show him the first page. Just a second. Could you read the last sentence of the last page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The above-mentioned persons are banned from entering the territory of Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." Do you know why I asked that question? As we were working on disarming paramilitaries at that point in time in Brcko and in Bijeljina, as we could not have these persons prosecuted, these persons who came with official IDs of the Republic of Serbia, war uniforms and equipment that they purportedly got from the Serbian MUP, we deported these persons from Brcko and Bijeljina. We boarded them on buses, and we brought them, unarmed, to Raca, to the border with Serbia, along with this list of persons who we were sending back. That is why I asked whether perhaps some of these persons had been banned from entering. These were persons who came as paramilitaries or formations sent by the MUP. I'm referring to the Red Berets. That's why I asked who prohibited this, because the MUP of the Republic of Serbia later also banned certain persons from going to Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 19541.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, let us see what my attitude was towards the military judiciary and what kind of pressure I exerted. 19541, 65 ter. So on the 1st of January, 1994, to the Ministry of Defence and to the president of the Supreme Military Court. Do you see this text?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Our hitherto acquired knowledge and official reports on the activities of the military prosecution in Bijeljina testify to numerous flaws, which primarily refer to the release from custody of persons detained under reasonable suspicion of having committed grave criminal offences, carrying severe penalties. "Such omissions have contributed to the deterioration of the general security and political situation in Brcko and Bijeljina. "The situation demands that an inspection of work of the Military Prosecutor's Office in Bijeljina be conducted immediately and that possible errors or criminal offences of not undertaking the necessary actions on the part of the prosecution be established. "It is your duty to act in line with the inspection's findings and inform me thereof."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time I see this. It is 1994, but the period when I was there was 1992 and the times were different. That was the beginning of the war and all of this that was happening in 1992. As for this that you wrote up in 1994, my hat is off to you, and I congratulate you on having done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 1st of January, 1994 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Your questions were not properly reflected in the transcript. What was your first question in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whether Mr. Davidovic knew that I had exerted this kind of pressure on the military judiciary, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And your second question was about the date of this letter?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Davidovic said that this was 1994. However, this pertains to 1992 and 1993, because this was the 1st of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Isn't that right, Mr. Davidovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I spoke about the period of 1992, the beginning of the war, when paramilitaries came to Bosnia, and when institutions were just being established, and when work was only starting.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could this please be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1419, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2752, could we have that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we are on the subject of my attitude towards the judiciary, and at this point in time the military judiciary, do you see that this is the 7th of August, 1994, on the authority that I --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a duplicate of 65 ter 22019, and we could see, then, the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. Let's up-load it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you release it? It hasn't been released.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It seems not working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then I'm going to ask you, Mr. Davidovic, to confirm or deny that this is a document asking for speeding up the procedure involved. We sent a document earlier on, asking about the case of the commander of the Brod Battalion, and then the second paragraph, it says: "Since we have been informed by the top judiciary organs of the republic that the case has not yet reached the judiciary organs, we ask you to urgently inform us about measures taken and about the stage that has been reached." And it signed by Gordan Milicic, on the authority of the president, the adviser for security.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter: We did not hear the question and we did not hear the beginning of the answer. This is too fast.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, just a second. You started answering too quickly, so the interpreters couldn't hear it all. And they also didn't hear the last part of your question, Mr. Karadzic. Could you check whether it's reflected or not?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The text was read out very fast, so we only did a sight translation of the text. We did not hear the question at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, but for you to put the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say here that this reflects an effort made to establish rule of law. Do you agree that this is an urging with the judiciary on the basis of the fact that we had heard that some things had not arrived yet?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, this document or this kind of urgent document that is being sent in order to have things speeded up shows that an effort is being made to establish legality. It is 1994, and it should be pointed out that as time went by in Republika Srpska, in certain segments the authorities started functioning, in part. That's for sure.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification as Exhibit D1420.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D3774. There is a translation. 1D3774.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at this, addressed to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska: "Confidential, deliver immediately," and then there is a stain. A request is made to submit a short progress report on the work of military disciplinary courts, specifying the number of disciplinary violations and the measures and sanctions, taken the problems and shortcomings in exercising jurisdiction and proceedings before military disciplinary courts. Do you agree that this is an effort to re-assert the rule of law?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1421, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2736 now, please. Could we zoom in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Radovan Karadzic hereby requests the Supreme Military Court of Republika Srpska and the Supreme Military Prosecutor's Office of Republika Srpska to explain why the trial is scheduled for 26 September 1994, while the accused are free? The first three accused -- sorry, the first seven accused --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters kindly ask Mr. Karadzic to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Seven --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You have to slow down. They lost you again, you're so fast. Start from: "The first seven accused ..."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought they could see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Seven of the accused spent only three days in remand, and three of the major accused spent only 30 days. That's all the investigating judge could do, because the military prosecutor did not submit a motion to remand in custody. Such gross omissions should not occur. And now I have to intervene with the translation. The translation should properly read "must not occur," not "should." Do you agree that the third paragraph says the judiciary must not allow - not "should," but "must" - not allow persons accused of murder to await trial at liberty, nor that in a period of imminent threat of war, a full 15 months elapsed from the time of murder until the beginning of trial? Do you agree, Mr. Davidovic, that I cannot interfere in the judgement, but I do interfere with their being at large?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. This is an effort to restore the rule of law. But how all this came about, I don't know. I can't comment. When they were -- when there was unrest in Banja Luka and there was general discontent because people accused of murder were at large, there was public dissatisfaction. And perhaps that caused you to write this document, in response to this unrest, or maybe this was something regular of your own initiative. If the latter, I can only welcome it and congratulate you. But, remember, there were roadblocks and barricades. The army was very unhappy. There were killings, suspects being released from prison. There was general discontent, and perhaps you wrote this under this pressure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For your information, September 1993 was resolved by police means, and nobody was tried. This is a regular thing, and it's about murders. Does that make you happy?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the witness has already said that he does not know about this particular, and he isn't sure whether it refers to a particular situation, or whether this was routine, that it was done frequently. What we have here is a reference to a particular case that the witness cannot help us with, so I do not think that this is the right person to get this document admitted through. We should know about that case, and why this particular letter was sent, and whether it was related to just this particular case and not, in general, the attitude at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you like to respond, or should I ask Mr. Robinson to help you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last paragraph. [In English] Just pay attention to the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I think you already understand the point that this is refuting the witness's testimony that no efforts were made to punish people, and, in fact, that Dr. Karadzic, himself, had personally seen to it had people were released. And here is evidence showing that, in fact, he is encouraging authorities in various cases to enforce the rule of law and to keep people detained. So I think it's very relevant to this witness's testimony and it ought to be admitted. It's perhaps something that the witness has no personal knowledge of, but it's definitely relevant to the subject of his testimony and directly contradicts it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I can only add that the last paragraph says that this applies generally to all proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Separate from the weight to be given in relation to this document, in particular in relation to the witness's evidence, the Chamber finds this document to be relevant, and we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1422, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, could you leave five minutes before the end of today's session so I can issue an oral ruling.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I also would need to state something in relation to an exhibit that was admitted, the one from Serbia. I can also do this after -- afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then shall we adjourn for today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I just deal with one more document related to this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3786.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That was my letter to the Supreme Military Prosecutor's Office and the Military Court. Do you agree that here, five days later, my adviser is addressing the Main Staff and repeating that the president of the republic makes it incumbent on the judiciary to urgently carry out an inspection and review of all cases involving murder, with priority given to crimes against life and limb, against war profiteering, and against property, and sanctions must be maximum? It must not be allowed that people accused of murder await trial at liberty and that unnecessary procrastination must not occur? Do you agree that this is addressed not only to the Military Office of the Prosecutor and the Supreme Military Court, but also to the Main Staff of the VRS, asking them to make sure that the decision involved is enforced?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that all this contributes to reinforcing the work of the judiciary.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, and then I won't go on because you need time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1423, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Davidovic. We will continue tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we need to go into private session to deal with your submission, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, that's not necessary. It is related to Exhibit D1416, the document from Serbia that we spoke about. And I said before there are no protective measures, and, indeed, there are no protective measures for the time being. However, this document was provided according to Rule 54 bis, and as it was disclosed only recently, the Republic of Serbia has not been informed about this, and they may perhaps want to ask protective measures. In particular, what they usually do is have the person -- the executive making the memo redacted and the recipients. Therefore, my proposal would be to have it temporarily under seal, and we will inform the Government of Serbia and inquire with them whether they want redactions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think there will be an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct. That's reasonable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll put it under seal for the moment. I think it's safer to go into private session to give this oral ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll rise and resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 30th day of June, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.00 p.m.,
